title: Countries are behind on money to protect nature
summary:
Nearly 200 countries promised to raise lots of money to protect oceans, forests, rivers and wildlife. So far, they have raised much less than they planned.

They will talk about this at a big United Nations meeting called COP17. It begins Monday in Yerevan, Armenia, and ends October 30. The meeting is about biodiversity, which means all the different kinds of plants and animals on Earth. The United States is not part of this treaty.

The countries promised $200 billion a year for nature by 2030. Each year from 2023 to 2025, they raised between $75 billion and $92 billion. That is less than half.

"We're not moving fast enough," said Astrid Schomaker, who leads the treaty's office.

There is some good news. The Philippines made an ocean area where people may not catch rays and sharks. Argentina made a new national park. Groups also plan to spend $500 million to help save threatened species.
why_it_matters: The animals and plants you see outside, and the clean water and air you need, depend on people protecting nature.
